title: Build a three-tier can pyramid on a shop display mat
instruction: Build a pyramid display of the six cans on the green mat: three in the bottom row, two on those, and one on top.
context: Shop staff build can pyramids for promotions. Each upper can rests across two cans below it, so the bottom row has to sit close enough for both supports, every can has to be set down upright and centred, and placing the upper tiers must not knock the ones already built.
setup: A light grey shop counter (90 x 100 cm). A green felt display mat (12 cm deep, 26 cm wide) is centred 32 cm in front of the arm bases, 12 cm left of their midline. Six identical cans (6.8 cm across, 6 cm tall, 300 g, flat ends) stand in a wooden delivery tray to the left, in two rows of three: 14 cm and 26 cm out, 29, 37 and 45 cm left of the midline. A shelf unit with four sauce bottles stands at the back, a yellow price card stands behind the mat and a blue shopping basket sits on the right.
scoring: 0 if any can ends tipped over (more than 45 degrees from upright). Otherwise, counting upright cans (under 10 degrees) by tier above the mat, one tier per can height (6 cm, rounded): 1.0 with three cans standing on the mat, two on those and one on top; 0.5 with the bottom two tiers (three and two) and none on top; 0.25 with exactly three cans upright on the mat and none above; 0 for anything else.
reset_notes: Return the six cans to the tray positions.
fidelity: Rigid bodies only. The cans are plain flat-ended cylinders; real cans have rims, which make bridging slightly less stable. Every surface has the same rubber-like friction (1.2).
